Cold mouth. Why the forehead?
Fast eater or slow?
The ice cream is in your
mouth.
So why does your
forehead hurt?
Your brain is not
freezing.
Look at the roof of your mouth.
The cold makes its blood
vessels clamp shut,
then flood wide open.
The nerve that reports
it also covers your
forehead,
so your brain blames
the wrong spot.
In one trial,
gulping it more
than doubled the chance
of getting one.
Doctors suggest pressing
your tongue to the roof
of your mouth,
to warm it back up.
